inventory.anchor: nsHttpChannel::OnBeforeConnect; nsHttpChannel::MaybeUseHTTPSRRForUpgrade; nsHttpChannel::ContinueConnect; nsHttpChannel::SpeculativeConnect; nsHttpChannel::OpenCacheEntryInternal; nsHttpChannel::IsForcedOffline (new)
inventory.notes: REGRESSION CONFIRMED: IsForcedOffline() (nsHttpChannel.cpp:8523) is a stub that returns false. The five call sites (OnBeforeConnect, MaybeUseHTTPSRRForUpgrade, ContinueConnect via a local, SpeculativeConnect, OpenCacheEntryInternal) no longer read bc->Top()->GetForceOffline(), so a forced-offline BrowsingContext no longer fails HTTP requests. The stub's own comment (reason: BrowsingContext ForceOffline field 'not landed yet') is WRONG for this tree: the field exists in Mozilla 157 itself (docshell/base/BrowsingContext.h:289 FIELD(ForceOffline, bool), accessor :684; webidl dom/chrome-webidl/BrowsingContext.webidl:159) and is still read by dom/base/Navigator.cpp:615 and dom/base/nsGlobalWindowInner.cpp:5188. It is set by juggler/TargetRegistry.js:697 (updateForceOffline), juggler/protocol/BrowserHandler.js:227-228, and also by devtools/server/actors/target-configuration.js:542 and remote/webdriver-bidi/modules/root/emulation.sys.mjs:726, so stock DevTools/BiDi offline emulation is broken too. Fix at the source: drop this whole diff (and the nsHttpChannel.h declaration) so the file equals Mozilla's; nothing here is needed, since the removed code compiled in 157. The comments name a third-party project and a docs path; rewrite or delete.

verifier.why: regression confirmed and cause corrected: the BrowsingContext ForceOffline field exists in Mozilla 157, so the stub is unnecessary
